title: Foods That Reduce Acid Reflux and Support Better Digestion
description: Put out the fire. Natural remedies and foods to soothe heartburn and improve gut motility.
content:
Acid reflux (GERD) feels like too much acid, but it is often a mechanical issue—the valve (LES) between stomach and esophagus relaxing when it shouldn't. Or, it can be caused by low stomach acid causing fermentation and upward pressure. Regardless of the cause, certain foods act as 'demulcents' (soothers) or buffers, coating the irritated lining and neutralizing excess burn without shutting down digestion completely.

Key Takeaways

  • Oatmeal absorbs stomach acid and is low in irritants.
  • Ginger is a pro-kinetic, moving food out of the stomach faster so it can't reflux.
  • Alkaline foods (melon, banana) help neutralize pH naturally.
  • Aloe Vera juice reduces inflammation in the esophagus.

Why It Matters

Chronic reflux can damage the esophagus. Relying solely on acid-blockers can impair nutrient absorption long-term. Using food to manage symptoms improves quality of life and sleep immediately while addressing gut health.

The Oatmeal Buffer

Starting the day with oatmeal is a classic reflux remedy. The gelatinous texture of cooked oats coats the stomach lining, and the fiber absorbs acid. Avoid adding heavy cream or acidic fruit; stick to almond milk and bananas.

Alkaline Fruits

Most fruit is acidic (citrus), but Melon (Cantaloupe/Honeydew) and Bananas are alkaline (pH > 5). Eating these can help buffer stomach contents. Fennel is another alkaline vegetable that has been used for centuries to soothe digestion.

Ginger Tea

Ginger strengthens the LES valve and speeds up gastric emptying. If food moves down into the intestines quickly, it can't come back up. Sip warm ginger tea (fresh root is best) after meals.

Workflow

  1. Small Meals: Overeating is the #1 trigger. The stomach stretches and pushes acid up. Eat until 80% full.
  2. The 3-Hour Rule: Do not lie down for 3 hours after eating. Gravity keeps acid down. Stop eating at 7 PM if you sleep at 10 PM.
  3. Left Side Sleeping: Sleep on your left side. Anatomically, this keeps the stomach below the esophagus, making reflux physically difficult.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is peppermint good?

No! Peppermint relaxes the LES valve, making reflux *worse*. It is good for lower gut gas, but bad for heartburn.

Does milk help?

It creates temporary relief but stimulates more acid production later (rebound). Almond or oat milk is a safer buffer.
